body_markdown:
The next Formula 1 Grand Prix could take place in your living room. Hot Wheels has added the entire 2026 Formula 1 grid to its catalog of 1/64-scale cars, including the two newest teams to join the series, and the models will be sold individually or as a set.


Hot Wheels inked a partnership with Formula 1 in 2024, and it released[the cars that raced in the 2025 season](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hot-wheels-races-into-2025-with-formula-1/) shortly after. The 2026 season[brought a major redesign](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/formula-1-will-sound-like-this-in-2026/) that included a smaller chassis, narrower tires, and several aerodynamic updates, and the scaled-down versions of the single-seaters receive these changes as well. Hot Wheels updated each car’s proportions and livery.


The latest batch of cars features a metal body and chassis, Real Rider tires, and a display plinth, and they’re sold in edition-specific collector packaging. They’re branded as “Premium” models, so they’re a step above regular Hot Wheels cars bound for the toy box. Shown above, the 2026 collection includes 22 cars from 11 teams—each Formula 1 team races two cars at every Grand Prix.


Retailers nationwide will begin receiving the Hot Wheels 2026 Formula 1 cars in 2027. Suggested pricing starts at $9.99 for individual cars and $24.99 for a two-car pack that includes both drivers from a single team. If you want the full grid, you can buy the Season Display Set (which includes a double-side display mat) for $220 from the Mattel Creations site starting on December 4, 2026. Hot Wheels will also expand its catalog of track sets in 2027, with the new additions ranging from $28.99 to $149.99.


At about $10 per car, we’re a long way from the cheap-and-cheerful Hot Wheels cars you find by the hundreds at the supermarket. The brand doesn’t want to alienate its core buyers, so it’s also releasing a range of Silver Series Tooned Formula 1 cars aimed at kids. Pictures haven’t been released yet, but we’re told that these cars stand out with “exaggerated proportions and bold styling,” though they retain the team and sponsorship logos and driver-specific colors seen on the real car. They’re priced at $3.99 each.


The post[The Full 2026 Formula 1 Grid Joins the Hot Wheels Catalog](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hot-wheels-2026-formula-1-grid-cars-pricing-availability/) appeared first on[Hagerty Media](https://www.hagerty.com/media) .
